ingredients.item: boneless beef short rib or chuck flap, sliced 5 mm against the grain
toasted sesame seeds, plus more to finish
Steamed rice , lettuce ssam, ssamjang , gireumjang as the purist dip, kimchi

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Charcoal or cast-iron at medium-high. The slices go on in a single layer, and because there is almost no sugar, the grill boss's job is color, not lacquer-management: leave them until the edges weep and the underside is browned, about 2 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the smell should be sesame and garlic over browning beef — a quieter grill smell than the sweet marinades, and the honest one for this cut.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Flip once, 90 seconds more, pull when the raw red is just gone at the center of the slice. Rest the batch 1 minute on a warm plate — galbisal is thin enough that carryover is quick and real.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: eating test straight off the grill: beef first, garlic second, sesame after. If you taste marinade before meat, the soy ran heavy — pull back a teaspoon next batch.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Scissors into bite pieces, warm platter, sesame over, ssam station open. The purist dip here is gireumjang (#SA02) — sesame oil, salt, pepper — because it seasons without competing; ssamjang (#SA01) for the bolder table.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the ssam test: leaf, gireumjang, galbisal, fold — and it should taste like the steakhouse version of Korean grill, clean enough that the beef's quality is the headline. Buy the good beef for this one; there is nowhere to hide.

storageNotes: Marinated slices keep 24 hours refrigerated. Cooked, 3 days — cold slices over rice with a fried egg and the leftover gireumjang is the intended day-after move.
Variations: a teaspoon of gochugaru in the marinade for a slow heat; the mushroom-soy build (#M02) swaps in cleanly; the bone-in flanken fork (#M03) when the table wants the full ceremony.
